sentences.text: Borealosuchus was a mid-sized crocodyliform, with the species B. wilsoni reaching approximately 3.2 to 4.5 meters in length.
The species B. acutidentatus has been estimated to have reached nearly 7 meters in length.
The specific name of the species B. threeensis references Exit 3 of the New Jersey Turnpike, which is the closest highway exit to its type locality.
The genus Borealosuchus was named by Christopher Brochu in 1997 to reclassify several species previously assigned to the genus Leidyosuchus.
A sixth species, B. threeensis, was formally named in 2012.
Fossils of the species B. threeensis were found in the Inversand Company Marl Pit in Gloucester County, New Jersey.
The species B. formidabilis is particularly well-known due to the discovery of remains from many individuals at the Wannagan Creek site in North Dakota.
While earlier studies suggested Borealosuchus belonged to Crocodylia, recent research classifies it as a basal eusuchian that does not belong to Crocodylia.
Borealosuchus fossils date from the Campanian to Priabonian stages, spanning from 83.6 to 33.9 million years ago.
